# Setup

Install Node 22, then run `npm install` in the repository root. The first install takes about 2 minutes.

## Environment

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in the workspace URL. The handbook builds without it, but the links to the live workspace stay empty.
Runs the 178 client-side rules by default. Two optional LLM passes
run via the codex CLI:

  low   sentence-tier semantic analysis, 40 rules
  high  low + document-tier structural analysis, 8 rules

Choose one with --llm-effort (off|low|high|auto), or use the sugar aliases:
  --llm       → --llm-effort=low
  --llm-deep  → --llm-effort=high
  --no-llm    → --llm-effort=off

$SLOP_COP_LLM takes the same four values and applies when no flag does.
When the codex CLI is on $PATH, --llm-effort=auto resolves to 'low';
otherwise 'off'. Auto-enabled passes fail open (the
failure is reported under 'llm.<tier>.error' and the client-side results
are still returned); explicit passes propagate the error as exit code 3.

Input is taken from the path argument, or from stdin when the path is "-"
or omitted.

Language-aware mode masks non-prose regions of the input before detectors
run, so slop-cop flags prose only — not code, tags, URLs, or other syntax.
Pick a mode with --lang:

  auto      (default) pick from the file extension; "text" for stdin.
  text      no masking; treat input as plain prose.
  markdown  CommonMark; mask code fences, links, HTML, YAML front matter.
  html      HTML; mask tags, attributes, <script>/<style>/<pre>/<code>.
  jsx,tsx   JS/TS with JSX; keep comments, strings, template quasis, JSX text.
  ts,js     JS/TS without JSX.

Suppressions inside masked modes drop structural false positives
(e.g. 'dramatic-fragment' on headings, 'staccato-burst' across list items).

The 226 rules come in three layers, all on by default. Pick with --standard:

  all     (default) every layer.
  slop    the original LLM-tell catalogue: does this sound like an LLM?
  base    the plain-language base layer: can this be read once and understood?
  google  the Google developer documentation style guide.

The selection applies to the LLM passes too — a layer left out never reaches
the prompt.

Individual rules are suppressed by a .slopcop.toml resolved by walking up from
the input path (--config overrides it):

  disable = ["colon-elaboration"]
  enable_only = ["overused-intensifiers"]

  [[overrides]]
  paths = ["docs/**/*.md"]
  disable = ["unformatted-code-identifier"]

Use --lines to report only the violations that begin within a 1-based inclusive
line range, while still scanning the whole document for context — useful for
linting just the lines an edit touched:

  50:80  a closed range          50:  from line 50 to EOF
  :80    from line 1 to line 80  50   a single line

mkdir -p scripts && cat > .slopcop.toml <<'EOF'
# Only the slop layer: "does this sound like an LLM?". The base and google
# layers are style-guide rules and flag text that is fine today.
[[overrides]]
# These rules are tuned for English punctuation. In German and French the
# dashes and colons are ordinary quotation and dialogue marks.
paths = ["docs/de/**/*.md", "docs/fr/**/*.md"]
disable = ["em-dash-pivot", "colon-elaboration", "question-then-answer"]
EOF
cat > scripts/lint-prose.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fail when README.md or any page under docs/ reads like LLM-written text.
# Rules live in .slopcop.toml. Needs the slop-cop CLI on PATH.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if ! command -v slop-cop >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "lint:prose: slop-cop not found on PATH (brew install yasyf/tap/slop-cop)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

status=0
while IFS= read -r file; do
  if ! out=$(slop-cop check "$file" --standard=slop --no-llm --strict --format=compact); then
    echo "== $file"
    echo "$out"
    status=1
  fi
done < <(find README.md docs -name '*.md' | sort)

[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "lint:prose ok"
exit "$status"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/lint-prose.sh
sed -i '' 's|"test": "node -e \\"console.log('"'"'tests ok'"'"')\\""|&,\n    "lint:prose": "bash scripts/lint-prose.sh"|' package.json
cat package.json; npm run lint:prose 2>&1 | tail -15; echo "exit ${pipestatus[1]}"
mv docs/guide.md /tmp/guide.bak; npm run lint:prose >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "without bad file exit $?"; mv /tmp/guide.bak docs/guide.md
